title: Model-specific concurrency caps with urgency tiers and graceful downgrade profiles
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Provide per-model concurrency limits and an urgency-tier admission path for Dedicated pools so that latency-sensitive traffic (interactive/low-latency) maintains SLOs during contention while batch/low-priority traffic is queued, delayed, or softly degraded.

Background: Dedicated pools today apply coarse-grained admission and autoscaling which makes it difficult to protect latency SLOs for critical models when bursty background workloads start consuming capacity. Customers want predictable P50/P95/P99 for specific model routes and the ability to declare urgency on requests.

Scope:
- Add per-model concurrency caps (configurable by model-version and route).
- Introduce three urgency tiers on the ingress path: urgent, normal, background.
- Implement a lightweight admission shim that enforces (concurrency cap + token-rate limit) per model and tier.
- Provide soft-downgrade policies: queueing with backpressure, fallback to smaller/quantized model variant, or preemptible deficit scheduling for background jobs.
- Integrate with Dedicated autoscaler: ensure scale-up reservations for urgent tiers and cooldown windows to avoid oscillation.

Design summary:
- Admission enforcement will be two-stage: (1) short-circuit fast-path semaphore for concurrency cap; (2) leaky-bucket token-rate gate for sustained throughput control. Semaphores are per model-shard and aggregated at pool-level to prevent cross-shard starvation.
- Urgency tiers map to different admission parameters and headroom reservations: urgent gets small reserved headroom across pool nodes; normal competes for remaining capacity; background is happiest-path for queued execution or immediate fallback.
- Graceful downgrade profiles are per-route policy objects: e.g., [queue for 200ms -> fallback to model-x-quant4 -> enqueue for up to 2s] with observable decision traces.
- Autoscaler hooks: when urgent-tier rejection rate exceeds 2% sustained for 30s, autoscaler fast-path triggers warmup provision of N additional replicas (configurable), with a 3-minute cooldown and linear backoff to prevent thrash.

Metrics and observability: Emit per-route metrics: concurrency_in_use, concurrency_limit, tier_rejections, tier_queue_time_ms, fallback_count, autoscaler_triggers. Add tracing annotations for admission decisions to the Console and per-route dashboards.

Trade-offs considered:
- Using only token-rate vs semaphore: token-rate alone protects steady-state throughput but cannot bound concurrent KV cache pressure; semaphore plus token-rate gives both latency and cost control at expense of slightly more complex bookkeeping.
- Reserved headroom increases cost but buys latency isolation for urgent traffic. We propose conservative defaults and allow customers to tune.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Per-model concurrency cap config deployable via Dedicated pool config API.
- Urgency header (X-Redwood-Urgency) accepted by API and enforced end-to-end.
- Under synthetic contention test, P99 latency for urgent tier remains within target (<= 250ms increase over baseline) while normal/background degrade as per policy.
- Dashboard shows admission decisions and fallback events.
- Rollout plan validated in staging and can be toggled per-pool.

Rollout: Start with a soft opt-in flag per pool, monitor, then enable default conservative caps for new Dedicated customers.

release_note: Introduce model-level concurrency and urgency tiers to improve latency isolation for Dedicated pools; configurable soft-fallbacks and autoscaler hooks included.
acceptance_criteria: Per-model concurrency limits configurable and enforced in staging
Urgency header accepted and enforced; metrics emitted for all decision types
P99 latency degradation for urgent tier within target under synthetic contention
Fallback flows execute and are visible in Console traces
